sentences.translation: Ohthere said to his lord, King Alfred, that he lived the furthest north of all Norwegians.

analysis.historicalNote: The long front vowel ǣ is characteristic of Old English spelling.

review.notes: Segmentation and source gloss follow the first \gll entry. Source: references/Voyages_of_Ohthere_Wulfstan.tex.
The dative singular is represented as an inflection, not a verb conjugation. Source: references/Voyages_of_Ohthere_Wulfstan.tex.

analysis.historicalNote: þ represents the thorn letter, pronounced like modern English th.

sentences.translation: He said that he lived in the northern part of the land by the West Sea (ocean west of Norway).

review.notes: The source gloss uses sjv.sg; the model expands this to subjunctive singular. Source: references/Voyages_of_Ohthere_Wulfstan.tex.

sentences.translation: He said though that the land continues very long to the north from there, but it is all uninhabited, except in a few places here and there Finns (i.e. Sami) camp, hunting in winter and in summer fishing by the sea.

analysis.historicalNote: The long front vowel ǣ is characteristic of Old English spelling.
